title: Built a golf course tycoon game with Claude. Looking for feedback.
author: powderbasket
selftext:
I've been building **Pine Hollow**, a mobile-first tycoon game where you buy the worst nine-hole muni in the county and try to turn it around. Trailer attached. 

**What it is:** a zoomed-out map in the style of the pocket tycoon games. Every golfer is simulated with a name, a handicap and opinions. They book tee times, play every shot (sand shots and lost balls in the pond included), buy a hot dog at the turn, and write a review based on what actually happened in their round. You set prices, hire a superintendent and crew, restore the clubhouse, add a pro shop that sells hats with your logo, and commission an architect who renders redesigned holes (island greens, doglegs, a boulder in the fairway). There's a slow-mo ace cam, charity scrambles, a yearly club championship, a junior prospect to mentor, and seasons.

**How AI was used:** the whole game was built in conversation with Claude. I played it, wrote notes, and Claude implemented them, round after round. It's a single HTML file of about 480KB with no engine and no image assets. Every sprite is drawn in code. For balancing, Claude wrote headless-browser test runs where bots play 30 days five different ways (spends everything, hands-off, overspends, makes random calls, plays normally), plus one run to year 3. They caught things like pace-of-play backups and an inbox bug that could answer the wrong question. They did not catch "this feels boring on day 20” which is why I'm here.

**What I'd love feedback on:** the first 15 minutes, whether money and upgrades feel too fast or too slow, the moment you quit and why, and any bugs (a screenshot plus your in-game day number helps).

Play in your browser here: https://claude.ai/artifact/3nA25CuWppqAhmKHNVNbSW 

It saves locally, and works best on a phone.  
Next up: the back nine, then a second course on land you buy.
